requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.xfs/mount sequence completed successfully; df and findmnt confirm /dev/mapper/vg_data-lv_data mounted at /srv/data (1.1G initial size). Given the disk was fully partitioned with no free space, the executor used loopback files as PV backing, a reasonable workaround for the constrained environment.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: Test files with recorded sha256 checksums were written before growth. vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs were run twice while /srv/data remained mounted (findmnt confirms continuous mount), growing the LV from 1.07G to 1.95G to a final 2.14G (2.1G in df, exceeding the 2GB requirement). sha256sum -c confirmed both test files unchanged immediately after the grow, directly demonstrating intact contents through a live online resize.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied: an LVM logical volume was created and mounted at /srv/data, then grown live from 1.1G to 2.14G while remaining mounted, with sha256 checksums confirming data integrity throughout. The separate node-restart evidence protocol was also executed well beyond the task's minimum bar: a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, mount, checksums) was captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged via connection drop, a differing post-restart boot_id was confirmed, and full recovery (service execution, VG reactivation, remount at correct size, checksum pass) was directly observed post-restart. This is corroborated by the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots (6bb7e004... to d6356ee2...).
limitations: Persistence across reboot was not an explicit requirement of the task instruction; it was performed to satisfy the separate provider-wide restart-evidence protocol and is scored independently.

The lifecycle collector's after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the executor_comparison diff, which is consistent with the executor's own reported timeline.

Loop device backing files reside on the root filesystem (/var/lib/lvmfiles); this is a reasonable workaround given the fully partitioned disk but was not independently confirmed as the only viable approach in this environment.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, every state-changing action ties to a clear purpose: dnf install lvm2 (prerequisite), fallocate/losetup (necessary PV backing given no free disk space), pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs/mount (core outcome), test file writes (needed to verify integrity across the grow), the two-step vgextend/lvextend/xfs_growfs (live grow to target size), and the systemd unit + fstab entry (required so the loop-backed VG can reactivate at boot, supporting the mandated restart-evidence protocol since loop devices are not otherwise reattached automatically). No troubleshooting dead-ends or unrelated mutations were found. Minor low-risk residue was left: /etc/fstab.bak (a defensive backup before editing fstab, standard practice) and /tmp/dnf.log, /tmp/reboot.log (command output redirects). These are trivial, non-destructive, and pose no functional or security risk, so they only lightly reduce the hygiene score. The final package-health and failed-services checks show no residue from the lvm2 install or restart.
